text.p: Annika Sorenstam, who won the LPGA Skins Game last week, enjoyed another big payday Sunday by pulling away for a three-stroke victory at the $600,000 Michelob Light Classic at Forest Hills Country Club.
Sorenstam, who shot an even-par 72 Sunday, took home the $90,000 first prize for her fourth victory and ninth top-10 finish in 12 events this year.
The 26-year-old Swede padded her lead atop the LPGA money list with $696,079, which does not include the $220,000 she won at the Skins Game.

"I've won four tournaments this year, and I'd like to win five or six," said Sorenstam, who will take a couple of weeks off to have wisdom teeth removed. "The Open is coming up, so I don't want to relax too much."
Hiromi Kobayashi of Japan was second at eight-under, stumbling to a final-round 74. Australian Karrie Webb was alone in third, four strokes back. It was her 10th top-10 finish in 11 events this year.
Sorenstam was steady if unspectacular in her final round, which she started with a one-stroke lead over Kobayashi.
Kobayashi remained one shot back after the turn, but came unglued in a three-hole stretch beginning at the par-4 10th.
On number 10, Kobayashi sent her tee shot right, and left her second shot short. She landed on the green in three and two-putted for bogey. Sorenstam parred.

Kobayashi fell three shots off the pace on 12 when her second shot landed in a bunker. She blasted out of the sand and two-putted from 23 feet for another bogey. Sorenstam gave a shot back on the 14th hole, where she two-putted from 10 feet, but Kobayashi failed to capitalise and bogeyed 16.
Kobayashi was disappointed with her play.
"Today, I was over-aiming," she admitted, "aiming too much over the break. You can see there's nothing wrong with Annika -- you can't expect her to miss."
